clause_name: Article IV, Section 1 — Termination of Agreement (para. A)
label: POSITIVE
reasoning_cat1: The wording itself is short and definite: an identified party, a defined trigger ("without cause"), a fixed notice period (90 days) and a required form (prior written notice). The only softness is that it is labelled paragraph "A" of a termination section and says nothing about the effect of termination on accrued pay, benefits or the pension contributions; but no single term in it carries two reasonable meanings. Modest probability only because "without cause" sits implicitly against a for-cause regime elsewhere and the paragraph does not say whether the 90-day notice can be shortened or paid out.
reasoning_cat2: This clause is the hinge of the instrument's outward-pointing provisions and is hard to harmonise with several of them. Article I fixes a definite term running from October 5, 2002 "through October 4, 2007," and Article II fixes a five-year maximum payable; a unilateral at-will exit conflicts in operation with that fixed-term structure. Article IV Section 3 supplies a review and appeal process for "corrective action or terminat[ion] for cause," Article V Section 13 permits immediate termination on restriction of medical staff privileges, and Article V Section 15 gives the County a separate 30-day non-appropriation termination right — so termination rights are scattered across Articles IV and V without any priority or "notwithstanding" language reconciling them, and this paragraph (A) plainly presupposes companion paragraphs it does not reproduce. That is a genuine whole-instrument coherence problem about who may end the contract, on what notice, and with what review.

clause_name: Article V, Section 11 — Enforcement of Remedies
label: POSITIVE
reasoning_cat1: Two textual features raise the risk. First, the cumulation language is entirely one-sided: it preserves only rights "conferred on or reserved to County," saying nothing about the physician's remedies, so a court is invited to read it as excluding (expressio unius) or as merely silent about the physician's remedies. Second, the catch-all string — "any other right or remedy herein or by law or equity provided or permitted ... now or hereafter existing by law or in equity or by statute or otherwise" — ends in an open "or otherwise" whose reach against the enumerated sources is uncertain. Those are namable general-vs-specific and one-sided-drafting tensions, though the sentence's core meaning (remedies are cumulative, not exclusive) is clear.
reasoning_cat2: The clause exposes conflict with the instrument's other remedial machinery. Article IV Section 3 channels "review and appeal of the decision to impose corrective action or terminate for cause" into the Faculty Practice Board policy or the medical staff bylaws — a procedure that reads as the applicable route, while this section preserves every remedy "concurrently" and thus arguably lets the County bypass it. It also overlaps with Article V Section 17 (non-waiver), which separately says the County may "invoke any remedy available ... under this Agreement or by law or in equity," duplicating and potentially varying this section. Its County-only orientation also sits awkwardly with Article V Section 4's instruction that the Agreement be construed as jointly prepared and against neither party.
